clue.text: Complaint about this old-style tribesman

indicators.note: about means going round, so the complaint word is wrapped around the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to complain, so a moan is a complaint
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about an old-fashioned member of a tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the Latin word hic, a classical convention. The tribe is known from the novel The Last of the Mohicans.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the past, famous from Fenimore Cooper's novel, so a historical tribal warrior.

clue.text: Detail 10 and 11 to symbolize this steel-maker

definitions.text: Detail 10 and 11 to symbolize this steel-maker

parts.words: Detail 10 and 11 to symbolize this steel-maker
parts.note: the tails, last letters, of the answers at 10 and 11 across together give a chemical symbol for a metal used in making steel

explanation.surface: Instructions to assign two items to represent a steelworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across ends in M and 11 across ends in N; Mn is the chemical symbol of this element, which is added to steel to harden it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey metallic element alloyed into steel for strength, whose symbol is Mn.

clue.text: Boy with one objection to fish

parts.note: Hal is a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A lad has a single complaint about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: She is the lowest of her sex

definitions.text: She is the lowest of her sex

parts.words: She is the lowest of her sex
parts.note: among women's singing voices this one is the deepest in pitch

explanation.surface: A woman who has sunk lower than any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowest' suggests moral baseness; it means the deepest singing voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female singing voice, or a singer with that range.

clue.text: A poem without a point?

indicators.note: without means the second letter a is taken out

parts.note: an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A pointless poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a poem with no point; drop the A from AN ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a point where lines or branches meet.

clue.text: Ecstatic words sung by a student

parts.note: the lyric of a song is its words
L is the learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student delightedly sings the words of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxing lyrical means talking with rapturous enthusiasm, so the adjective can mean effusive or rapturous.

clue.text: Fruit distributed by Byron — real good at first

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged
at first means only the first letter of good is used

explanation.surface: Lord Byron hands out fruit, and it is really good.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of raspberry and blackberry, a soft red fruit.

clue.text: Prepare 25, say, for banter

explanation.surface: Making a beef dish while exchanging jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 down is BEEF, a joint you might cook in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook meat in an oven, as with a beef joint; also, as a noun, a mocking teasing session.

clue.text: Ravines (Oriental) so described?

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, especially on the south coast of England
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Asks what name oriental ravines might have.
explanation.walkthrough: Chines are ravines, as on the Isle of Wight; add E for East and you have a word that itself means Oriental.
explanation.definitionFit: From China, an East Asian nation, hence oriental.

clue.text: Many a girl's proposition

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals, a large number
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Numerous girls receive a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposition' suggests an offer to a girl; it is the logical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, a subsidiary theorem proved on the way to a larger one.

clue.text: Singular cover for a member in many long sittings

indicators.note: in means the answer is tucked inside the run of letters of the words many long sittings

explanation.surface: A lone covering worn by one person through many long sessions, like a politician's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' asks for the singular of a word normally plural for stockings; the 'member' is a leg, not a Member of Parliament. 'sittings' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings of this synthetic fibre are called by its name, so one stocking covering a leg takes it in the singular.

clue.text: Boxer has practice without mat — what arrogance!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the practice word sits outside the mat

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
an ism is a doctrine or practice

explanation.surface: A boxer trains without a mat and shows great arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here has its old sense of outside, as in hymns, so the boxer and practice go round the mat. 'Boxer' is the dog breed, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatism is asserting opinions as certain truth, an overbearing, arrogant manner.

clue.text: A universal spring (Titian)

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
a burn is a Scottish stream, water rising from a spring

explanation.surface: A universal season, in the style of a famous Venetian painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titian' is the reddish-brown hair colour named after the painter, not the painter himself. 'spring' is not the season but water rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian red is a reddish-brown hair colour, much like the chestnut shade described by this word.

clue.text: Scholar follows stories about the accursed thing

indicators.note: follows puts the scholar word after the other pieces

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: An academic tracks down tales about a cursed object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here just means concerning; the stories word ANA is followed by THE and then MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formally cursed by the church, or an object of loathing, is described by this word.

clue.text: So the grand may become self-willed

indicators.note: may become means the letters can turn into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Thus the important people may become obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly determined to have one's own way.

clue.text: Former Liberal about to give praise

indicators.note: about means going round, so the former-and-Liberal letters enclose the small word

parts.note: ex means former

explanation.surface: An ex-Liberal politician is about to pay compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning 'going to', but 'about' wraps the former Liberal round the 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol something is to laud it highly.

clue.text: Plant not smoked at any time

parts.note: ever means at any time
green bacon is unsmoked bacon

explanation.surface: A plant that has never been smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain green bacon is bacon that has not been smoked; 'smoked' suggests tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or tree that keeps its leaves all year round.

clue.text: Swordsman, key fellow, organized a riot

parts.note: G is a musical key
a lad is a fellow

indicators.note: organized means the letters of a riot are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A swordsman, a key man, stirred up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges A RIOT into IATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena fighter armed with a sword.

clue.text: Near Yggdrasil perhaps — north, not south

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be reshuffled
north, not south means the letter for one direction replaces the other

parts.note: S is south
N is north

explanation.surface: Close to the world tree of Norse myth, northward rather than southward.
explanation.walkthrough: Yggdrasil is the giant tree of Norse myth. 'north, not south' swaps its S for N giving YGGDRANIL, which 'perhaps' rearranges. 'Near' means stingy, not close.
explanation.definitionFit: Near in the old sense of mean or tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Use the needle, and so heighten the narrative?

explanation.surface: A storyteller doing needlework spices up the story.
explanation.definitionFit: To sew decorative stitching on cloth; also to exaggerate or embellish a story.

clue.text: Good, when abroad, to restrain an impulse, bud!

indicators.note: to restrain means to hold in, so the foreign word holds the impulse

parts.note: bon is French for good
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to curb a sudden impulse, addressed as a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bud!' looks like a form of address to a pal; it is the verb meaning to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin to grow or sprout, as a plant puts out new shoots.

clue.text: Mimicking all but start of recording

indicators.note: all but the start means the first letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: taping is recording

explanation.surface: Copying the whole of a recording except its beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, so this is copying.

clue.text: Give rise to trendy example of church architecture

parts.note: in means fashionable
a spire is a tapering steeple on a church

explanation.surface: Fashionable church design gives rise to new ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt or stimulate a feeling or creative idea.

clue.text: Claim unjustly that Yorks town lacks 22 dn

indicators.note: lacks means the town's name is missing something

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire
the answer to 22 down is the name of the letter H

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town without a dropped letter makes a false claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down names the letter H, famously dropped in some accents; Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire, so dropping its H gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to seize or claim something without right.

clue.text: Dropped, perhaps — being a source of irritation

parts.note: an itch irritates the skin

explanation.surface: Something that was let fall becomes annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the name of the letter H, which many English speakers drop in speech ('ouse' for 'house').
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is famously left out by speakers of some accents, so it is something dropped.

clue.text: Consented to renounce source of such avarice

definitions.text: Consented to renounce source of such avarice

indicators.note: to renounce means to give up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: agreed means consented

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of avarice

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to give up the root of their avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop A, the first letter of avarice, from AGREED; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is excessive desire for wealth, the vice also called avarice.

clue.text: Exhalation from mother of Hermia ? Not her

indicators.note: not her means those three letters are taken away

parts.note: Hermia's ma is her mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breath from the mother of Shakespeare's Hermia, but not from Hermia herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother of Hermia' is read as HERMIA'S MA; 'Not her' drops HER from the front. Hermia is a heroine of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour given off by rotting matter, an unhealthy exhalation.

clue.text: Complaint: encountered initially among Gort's men

indicators.note: among means the single letter goes into the soldiers' abbreviation

parts.note: the BEF, the British Expeditionary Force, was led by Lord Gort in 1939-40

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of encountered

explanation.surface: A grievance first met among the soldiers of a general.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gort commanded the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) in France in 1939-40.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Some soldiers take warning as a result

parts.note: the RE, the Royal Engineers, are some soldiers
fore is the golfer's shouted warning

explanation.surface: A group of soldiers heeds a warning, and acts accordingly.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'Fore!' is shouted on a golf course to warn of a ball in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb means consequently, for that reason.

clue.text: Chord — one in a form of jazz

indicators.note: in means the letter for one is put inside the jazz word

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chord used in a style of jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a three-note chord: root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Kind of expression resulting from a bad name?

definitions.text: Kind of expression resulting from a bad name?

parts.words: Kind of expression resulting from a bad name?
parts.note: the proverb says give a dog a bad name and hang him, so the look follows from that

explanation.surface: A facial expression caused by a poor reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'give a dog a bad name and hang him' supplies both halves of the compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamefaced, guilty look, as of a dog expecting punishment.

clue.text: Phoney item from Vulcan's place by the railway

parts.note: Vulcan, Roman god of fire, worked at a forge
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A fake object from the smithy next to the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeit document or artwork is a fake.
